description: Write the investigation report for issue #7597 as a markdown file at .agents/tasks/task-fleet-probe-coverage-investigation/INVESTIGATION.md. This is a diagnostic writeup, NOT a code change: the evidence supports the needs-investigation / CI coverage-arm truncation disposition. Do NOT add fleet_probe.py to any coverage baseline, and do NOT write redundant tests. The report must present the evidence, reach a disposition, and assess the separate CI-policy suggestion.
steps: Create .agents/tasks/task-fleet-probe-coverage-investigation/INVESTIGATION.md with sections: Summary, Evidence, Disposition, The 34/229 signature, CI truncation mechanism, Second suggestion (Coverage Gate on main), Recommendation.

Evidence 1 (tests exist): test/test_pipeline_conductor_agent.py has class TestFleetProbe (line 179) whose _mod() loads the script via load_skill_script('fleet_probe', SKILL_DIR / 'scripts' / 'fleet_probe.py') (line 181) and drives mod.main([...]) through ~25 tests. Cite the specific tests that exercise argument parsing (test_malformed_config_exits_2, test_typed_misconfiguration_is_malformed_config, test_nonfinite_numeric_config_is_malformed), output shaping (test_fired_lines_carry_metadata_never_transcript_text, test_protocol_tag_fires_and_working_stays_quiet), and failure paths (test_missing_transcript_reports_gone, test_corrupt_handled_map_degrades_to_empty, test_symlink_out_of_the_store_reads_gone, test_traversal_session_keys_are_malformed_config). These arrived in c0dca4a8b itself, so 'No commit since has added tests for it' does not hold.

Evidence 2 (load mechanism does NOT defeat coverage): test/skill_script_helpers.py::load_skill_script uses importlib spec_from_file_location and is not registered in sys.modules, but coverage.py attributes execution by file path via setup.cfg [coverage:paths] source = src/ . Prove the mechanism is fine by the control case: credit_spend.py lives in the SAME pipeline-conductor/scripts/ dir, is loaded by the SAME load_skill_script in the SAME test file (class TestCreditSpend), and is NOT in .github/coverage-baselines/backend.txt and passes the gate. ~14 skill scripts use this loader and none are baselined. So a near-zero reading for fleet_probe.py specifically is an anomaly, not a property of the load path.

Evidence 3 (not reproducible / one-run): git log for src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/pipeline-conductor/scripts/fleet_probe.py shows only c0dca4a8b; fleet_probe remains absent from .github/coverage-baselines/backend.txt; overall backend coverage was healthy at 91.68%. Combined with the auto-pipeline sampling (7 of 7 rebased-ahead PRs showed Coverage Gate: success), the 14.8% was one run, not a standing state.

Explain the 34/229 = 14.8% signature: 34 statements is close to what executes from the module TOP LEVEL alone (imports, module constants like PROTO/DEFAULT_ERR_RES/DEFAULT_BANNED_RES/_KEY_RE, and the def statement lines), with every function BODY unattributed. That is the fingerprint of the covering tests not landing in the coverage data that got combined - not of a file with no tests.

Document the CI truncation mechanism from .github/workflows/ci.yml: backend coverage runs only on the 3.12 shards (line ~692), sharded 4 ways via pytest-split, each shard uploads .coverage.<group> (lines ~699-716). ci.yml lines 581-583 self-document: 'The slowest 3.12 shard runs ~29 minutes, so a 30-minute cap kills the job at the coverage step with every test green and Coverage Gate then reds on the missing shard artifact.' The coverage-combine job (line ~973) downloads pattern coverage-shard-* with merge-multiple:true and has NO all-shards-present assertion, so it succeeds on partial data; coverage combine + coverage xml then produce a report where a file whose covering tests all ran in the lost shard shows only its import-time lines. This is the #7516 / PR #7517 class. Adding tests would not fix it; baselining would record a false rate for a covered file.

Assess the second suggestion precisely (do not overstate). The issue says Coverage Gate is 'effectively PR-only'. In fact ci.yml on: block (lines 3-6) triggers on BOTH push: branches:[main] and pull_request: branches:[main], so it is not PR-only by trigger. The real gap is the concurrency block (lines 11-19): cancel-in-progress is false on main, but the concurrency group permits only one pending run and GitHub evicts a pending run when a newer one queues, so with a ~19min run and ~1.4min median merge gap main gets only PERIODIC coverage verdicts, not one per commit - which is how a below-floor file can merge in a gap and surface later on a rebasing PR. State this as its own item and note it is a CI-policy matter worth a dedicated issue (per the auto-pipeline routing), distinct from this diagnosis.

State clearly in the report that empirical coverage measurement was BLOCKED by the sandbox network mode (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY): coverage and pytest-cov are not installed and cannot be installed from PyPI, verified. The disposition is reached by static analysis, which is conclusive given the control case (credit_spend.py) and the self-documented CI truncation mechanism.

Recommendation section: (1) Route #7597 to needs-investigation as a likely duplicate of the CI coverage-arm truncation class (#7516/#7517); do NOT add tests for fleet_probe.py and do NOT extend the baseline. (2) Track the sparse-main-coverage-verdict concern as its own CI-policy issue. Reference exact file:line evidence throughout so the report can be posted back to the issue and/or turned into a PR.
